transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess work is what made me finally come in. I’m a buyer, so I’m always looking at numbers and launch stuff and vendor sheets, and lately I just can’t shake this feeling that people at work — and even some of the vendors — are tracking what I buy and messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid.

My supervisor keeps showing me reports like, “See, it doesn’t show that,” but I don’t know… it still feels like something’s off. And the weird thing is, I used to be really good at spotting trends, like even in high school I could tell when people were trying to pull something, but this is different. It’s like I can’t let it go, and it’s making it hard to just do my job normally.
How long have you been feeling this way about people at work and vendors tracking or tampering with your numbers—has this been going on for days, weeks, or longer?

Um… it’s been longer than days. I think… like around ten months? It kind of started small, like I’d notice a number not matching and then I’d think, “Okay, that’s weird,” and then it just kept building.

And it’s not just the tracking thing — the voice has been around in that same stretch too, like roughly ten months. I know that sounds… I don’t know, but yeah, it’s been most of the past year.
Can you tell me more about this voice—what does it say, and does it talk about you as 'he' or comment on what you're doing, or does it feel more like it's speaking directly to you?

It’s… it’s usually like a man’s voice, not somebody I recognize exactly. Sometimes I’ll be in the stockroom, like pulling samples or checking boxes, and it sounds like it’s right behind me. It’ll say stuff like, “Move faster, Scott,” which is weird because that’s my name, obviously, and then I turn around and there’s nobody there.

Or when I’m driving back from a vendor meeting, it’ll kind of laugh, like at the stuff I picked, like I made a dumb choice. It feels more like it’s talking right to me, not like saying “he’s doing this” or whatever. I mean… sometimes it’s hard to tell because I’m already thinking about the meeting, and the traffic on the 5 is insane, and then I start replaying the whole conversation with the vendor, like whether they looked at me weird when I asked about quantities. But the voice part, yeah, it’s like it’s aimed at me.

Yeah, like I said, it’s usually in the stockroom or when I’m driving back from a vendor meeting. It sounds like a man’s voice, kind of right behind me, which is why I’ll actually turn around sometimes.

It’ll say, “Move faster, Scott,” or laugh like I picked the wrong stuff, like the samples or the buy was stupid. And then there’s nobody there. I know that sounds weird… it just feels really real in the moment.
Over these past ten months, have you noticed any changes in your motivation, energy, or interest in things you used to enjoy, or in how you interact with friends and family?

Yeah… I mean, I guess so. On my days off I mostly just sit in my apartment and scroll through sneaker drops, like the release pages and resale stuff, but I don’t even really care that much. It’s just something to look at.

My friends will text about volleyball or going to a gallery night or whatever, and I’ll see it, and then it feels like this whole thing to answer. Like I have to come up with the right words, then maybe I have to actually go, and it’s just… too much. So I don’t reply a lot of the time.
Have there been times in the past ten months when your mood and energy felt normal, but you still heard the voice or still believed people were tampering with your numbers?

Yeah… yeah, there was a stretch like that. Like, I wasn’t all revved up or anything. I was sleeping more normal, not feeling like I had to stay on top of every single thing in the market or like I could predict what was gonna sell before everyone else.

But even then, for a few weeks, I still thought people were tracking my buys, like watching the numbers or messing with them somehow. And I still heard the voice in the stockroom. It was confusing, because on the outside I probably seemed calmer, but that part didn’t really stop.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports persecutory delusions (belief that coworkers/vendors are tampering with numbers to sabotage him) and auditory hallucinations (a male voice commenting/commanding, 'Move faster, Scott,' laughing at his choices) persisting for approximately 10 months, well exceeding the 1-month threshold for schizophrenia and meeting the 6-month duration criterion. There is clear functional decline: social withdrawal from friends, anhedonia, and impaired occupational functioning as a buyer. Critically, the patient confirms a multi-week period of euthymic mood (normal sleep, no elevated energy) during which psychotic symptoms (delusions and hallucinations) persisted, ruling out a primary mood disorder with psychotic features (schizoaffective disorder or bipolar/depressive with psychotic features) as the psychosis is not confined to mood episodes. The hallucinations have both second-person commanding and commentary qualities, and delusions are persecutory in nature, consistent with schizophrenia paranoid-type presentation.
